SMTO-MON-0010 — This monitor command waits for someone to type

GUID: 41c51a92-1cc7-4f61-b140-c13e3969d596
Slug: monitor-command-interactive
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • The monitor's command starts a program that waits for a person, such as an editor, a remote login or top. Monitors run unattended, so SMTO didn't create this one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to use a command that prints its result and exits by itself, such as free -m instead of top. Each monitor run must finish on its own so its output can be recorded.
  2. For database or script tools, give the command up front: psql or mysql with -c or -e, python or node with -c, bash with -c. SMTO accepts these tools when the command to run is included, because they then finish without input.
  3. Don't use ssh, vim, nano, less or man in a monitor; ask the agent for a different read-only command. SMTO never accepts these programs as monitor commands, because they usually wait for someone to type.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the command, and the monitor starts recording readings.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the command, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same command unchanged; it will be rejected each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • monitor_command_rejection_reason rejected the command because its first command name is in _INTERACTIVE_COMMANDS (for example top, htop, vim, less, ssh or python) without a supported -c, -e or -lc command-mode exception.

What this means

  • The first command name belongs to the interactive-command set and lacks one of the supported explicit command-mode exceptions. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • The first command name belongs to the interactive-command set and lacks one of the supported explicit command-mode exceptions.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the command name and supported -c/-e command form rather than trying to supply terminal input to the monitor.

How to fix it

  • Use a noninteractive command that exits with captured output, or an allowed explicit form (mysql/psql with -c or -e, python/python3/node with -c, bash/zsh/fish with -c or -lc). For continuous output use watch -n or tail -f as a raw_stream with a positive duration. See src/agent_runtime/monitors/drafting.py.
  • Use a noninteractive captured command or a supported bounded stream.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported noninteractive observation runs within the monitor's captured execution contract.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
